name: Tamworth

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme in force yet. The council consulted from May to 20 August 2026 on licensing smaller HMOs with three or four occupants; no decision had been announced at the last check. HMOs with five or more occupants already need a mandatory licence.

housing: Tamworth is a compact borough that grew rapidly from the 1960s as an overspill town for Birmingham, so most homes are post-war and 1970s to 1980s estate houses. Private renting is below the West Midlands average and concentrated near the town centre and in former council houses bought under right to buy. The council knows of around 131 HMOs and has consulted on licensing smaller ones. Prices are below the regional average.
checkinTips: 1970s and 1980s estate houses in Belgrave and Stonydelph: photograph window seals, garages in blocks and shared paths and parking courts.
Former council houses bought under right to buy: check boilers, wiring and any non-standard construction noted on the paperwork.
Small HMOs near the town centre: record each bedroom lock and key, fire doors, alarms and the shared kitchen.
Victorian terraces near the castle: photograph back yards, rear walls and any damp in rear rooms.
Homes near the Rivers Tame and Anker: check ground floors and walls for damp or past flood marks.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Tamworth Borough Council's private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions.
